one_month_reasoning: No confirmed Nebius catalyst before Oct 31. The Q3-26 date is unannounced (the investor-events page lists nothing and EDGAR shows no new 6-K through Oct 1); Q1/Q2 were reported May 13 / Aug 12, so mid-November is most likely, with perhaps 15% odds of a late-October report (an unconfirmed third-party Oct 22 estimate). In the window: hyperscaler Q3 earnings and 2027 capex commentary (MSFT/META/GOOGL/AMZN, late October), which move AI-infrastructure names both ways; stock supply (Form 144s Aug-Sep, a 2026-09-29 Form 144, up to 12.3M ATM shares, holders of the 15.8M August exchange shares); and the 10-yr at 5.29% (+33bp in a week), a mild headwind for long-duration names. The Inferize deal (Oct 1) and Palantir partnership (Sep 8) are priced. I stay close to a symmetric lognormal around spot at ~29-30% monthly vol (106%/3.5), median ~$231, tilted very slightly lower for supply and rates; the small chance of an in-window report only widens the tails a little.

fair_value.method: Blend of a site-by-site cohort GPU-economics DCF (40%, $144/share probability-weighted; every inventory site valued once: signed contracts at their terms (Microsoft at Vineland, Meta 2025, Meta $12B dedicated, the Meta $15B backstop floor, Q2-26 neolab deals) discounted at 7.5-10.5%, everything else probability-weighted net of capex at a 12.5% WACC; single-rate DCF $140) and EV/NTM sales at Oct-2027 (60%, 4.2x on $23B NTM revenue less $15.6B net debt plus $3.65B stakes over 384M diluted shares = $220). Blended 12-month fair value about $190, ~18% below spot; DCF at a 5/7-yr economic life $125/$153.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Site-based cohort FCFF 2026Q4-2050 (round 4, replaces the aggregate GW path). Each of the 25 inventory sites is a set of slices with MW, energization year, ownership and contract: energized ~0.57 GW active at YE26 (Vineland 300, Mantsala 1 75, Kansas City 20, Longcross 20, Keflavik 10, Woodbury 10, Modi'in 8, Paris 5, plus ~0.2 GW delivering late 2026 at Bethune, Beit Shemesh, Masmiya, Estonia); named pipeline to 4.1 GW nominal / 3.4 GW probability-weighted by 2032 (Highridge PA 1.2 GW, Independence 1.2 GW, Lappeenranta 310, Birmingham 300, Bethune 240, Beit Shemesh 75, Mantsala 2 70, AIB 65, Oklahoma 50, UK 64, Estonia/Masmiya 29 each, Madrid 23), then 3%/yr generic growth. Contracts at their terms (customer pays Nebius): Microsoft $3.48B/yr ($11.6M/MW on Vineland 300 MW) to mid-2031 at 7.5%; Meta 2025 $2.9B/5 yrs (50 MW, Mantsala 1) at 7.75%; Meta $12B dedicated, 5 yrs from 2027 ($15M/MW, 160 MW at Mantsala 2 and Lappeenranta) at 8.5%; Meta $15B backstop as a $3B/yr 5-yr floor on Birmingham phase 1 (200 MW) at 9.0%; Q2-26 neolab/quant deals $22.5M/MW for 2.5 yrs (70 MW, Bethune) at 10.5%. Uncontracted capacity: vintage rates $15M (2026), $17.5/17.0/16.5M (2027-29), $15.5M long run, 80% on 3-yr terms, then the decay index 1.00/1.00/0.80/0.65/0.57/0.51/0.46/0.42; each pipeline slice multiplied by its build probability (0.5-0.95) with its capex. Costs: other opex 27% of revenue; owned sites power + site O&M $1.2M/MW-yr and facility capex $10M/MW; leased sites power + colocation $2.8M/MW-yr (rent fixed for the lease term) and no facility capex; IT capex $21.25M/MW; 6-yr economic life, refresh at full IT cost, 10% salvage. WACC 12.5% (Ke 13.1%) for uncontracted, post-contract and terminal flows; g 3%; less $7B deferred revenue, plus $6.7B pro-forma net cash and $3.65B stakes; 384M shares; +$2.4 asset-light option. Scenarios (split rate) bear $11 / base $133 (avg of $114 at x1.0 and $152 at x1.15 on uncontracted 2026-29 rates) / bull $291, weighted 25/50/25 = $142 + $2.4 = $144 (single rate $140). Sensitivities (weighted, split): life 5/7 yrs $125/$153; ERP 5.0% $126, 4.14% $155; IT capex -/+12% $162/$127; facility $8.5M/$12M $153/$134; decay supply-long $118, tight $177; long-run rate $14M/$17M $115/$174; 2027-29 at Q2 terms $179; Meta priced at $12M/$20M per MW $141/$149; contracted rates +/-1pp $143/$146; all sites built (p=1) $152.

inputs_detail.derivation: Midpoints of reaffirmed FY26 guidance: revenue $3.0-3.4B, adj. EBITDA margin ~40%, capex $20-25B; Q4 stub = $1.3B revenue, ~$7B capex.

Site model: Microsoft $3.48B + Meta 2025 $0.58B + Meta dedicated $1.06B (ramp) + Birmingham backstop $1.2B (ramp) + Q2-26 deals $1.58B + energized own-cloud $0.87B + late-2026 uncontracted deliveries $2.03B + 2027 deliveries (part-year, probability-weighted) $2.88B. Consensus $12.30B (StockAnalysis); RPO $37.5B with 36% recognised Jul-26 to Jun-28 as a floor. Round 3 capped 2027 at $14B; no cap needed now.

inputs_detail.input: Site capacity schedule (gross MW by site and year)
inputs_detail.value: YE26 active ~0.57 GW (not the 0.9 GW connected midpoint); in-service nominal / probability-weighted: 2027 1.71/1.63 GW, 2028 2.19/2.02, 2029 3.01/2.67, 2030 3.60/3.10, 2031 3.95/3.32, 2032 4.10/3.41; then +3%/yr generic growth (not tied to a site). Site phases: PA 260 (Oct-27) / +400 (Jan-29) / +340 (Nov-29) / +200 (2031); Independence 150/200/300/250/150/150 in 2027-32; Lappeenranta 90/100/120 in 2027-29; Birmingham 200 (2027) / 100 (2028); Bethune 120 (late 2026) / 120 (2027); AIB 32 (Aug-27) / 33 (Dec-27).
inputs_detail.derivation: Every MW comes from a named inventory site (sites.json), so nothing is counted twice and no site is missing. Phase dates from company project sites (PA, Birmingham, Independence), letters and landlord filings (AIB 8-K); IT-only allocations (Estonia, Harlow, Beit Shemesh, Masmiya, Madrid, AIB, UK) converted to gross at 1.3x. YE26 active power: the ARR guide $7-9B at ~$12M/MW implies 0.58-0.75 GW active (inventory flag F6), and the sum of energized sites plus late-2026 deliveries gives ~0.57 GW; capacity connected at Independence/Birmingham/PA in late 2026 earns from 2027. Named sites total ~4.1 GW against the 5 GW contracted-power target; the ~1 GW not tied to a named site is excluded (upside).

inputs_detail.input: Cohort contract rates (revenue per effective MW-year)
inputs_detail.value: Contracts fixed at their prices in every scenario (Microsoft $11.6M, Meta 2025 $11.6M, Meta dedicated and backstop $15M, Q2-26 deals $22.5M per MW-yr). Uncontracted vintages: legacy 2024/2025 $9-10M (Blackwell-class Longcross/Modi'in/Woodbury $12.5M); 2026 $15M; 2027 $17.5M, 2028 $17.0M, 2029 $16.5M; 2030+ $15.5M long run. Scenario multipliers on uncontracted 2026-29 rates x0.85 / x1.0-1.15 / x1.3; long-run rate now an explicit scenario variable: bear $13.0M, base $15.5M, bull $13.7M (equal lifetime revenue per MW to base on the tight decay curve).
inputs_detail.derivation: Q2-26 deals $20-25M/MW for capacity arriving late 2026 and older-gen pricing +30% QoQ support $15M for uncontracted 2026-vintage capacity (round 3's $12.5M 2026 cohort was a blend dominated by Microsoft at $11.6M, now modelled separately). Long-run $15.5M is the price at which a colocation-based marginal supplier earns ~15% on a refresh (site cost $2.8M/MW); Nebius's owned sites earn ~20% at that price because they avoid the rent. Supervisor round 3: this rate, not the life, drives the DCF ($14M $115, $17M $174), so it is shown as a scenario variable. Round 3's bull rate was IRR-calibrated ($13.6M); $13.7M keeps the same lifetime revenue per MW as base (5.31 x $13.7M = 4.69 x $15.5M).

inputs_detail.input: Contract coverage and term by cohort
inputs_detail.value: Signed contracts at their own term: Microsoft 5 yrs to mid-2031 (5.5 yrs from the 2026 vintage); Meta 2025 5 yrs to ~Jan-2031; Meta dedicated 5 yrs per order from 2027; Meta backstop 5 yrs from each cluster's deployment; Q2-26 deals ~2.5 yrs (1-3 yr mid-term). Uncontracted vintages: 2024 60%/2 yrs, 2025 80%/2 yrs, 2026+ and refreshes 80%/3 yrs, priced at the vintage rate for the term.
inputs_detail.derivation: Microsoft 6-K: five-year term, TCV ~$17.4B through 2031, tranches Nov-2025 to Aug-2026. Meta 6-K (Mar-2026): 5-year orders, $12B dedicated from early 2027, up-to-$15B backstop. Q4-25 letter: Meta 2025 clusters fully in servicing (Dec-2025/Feb-2026 tranches). Letter: mid-term contracts average 1-3 years. RPO $37.5B at 6/30/26 = Microsoft ~$16B + Meta ~$14.6B + Q2 deals >$4B + other.

inputs_detail.input: Post-contract / uncontracted revenue path (market index vs contract rate, by cohort age)
inputs_detail.derivation: Steep in the ~2 years after the next generation ships (a year after deployment at Nvidia's annual cadence), flatter after: SemiAnalysis H100 composite fell ~50% in 18 months after H200/B200 then held ~$2.80; relative to a contract price ~0.75x launch spot, that is ~-35% over ages 1-3, then ~-10%/yr. Checks: age 3 = 0.65/1.3 = ~50% of launch spot (H100 at 41-44%); age 6 = ~35% (A100 at 23-39%). Ornn: old chips reprice with the falling cost of compute (~$3/PFLOP-hr for A100/H100/B200), not to scrap. Bull reflects CoreWeave-style re-contracting at ~95%; bear the research's supply-long case where Hopper-class rents approach cash cost within 3-4 years.

Higher than round 3 because owned sites (>75% of capacity from 2028) no longer pay a colocation fee; their facility cost moves into capex and D&A (inventory flag F2). Nebius AI-cloud adj. EBITDA margin was 49.7% in Q2-26 with mostly leased capacity; other opex held at 27% of revenue for all customers, including dedicated hyperscaler capacity (prudent).

inputs_detail.input: Site costs by ownership (owned vs leased)
inputs_detail.value: Owned (Mantsala 1/2, Lappeenranta, Independence, Highridge PA, Birmingham): power + site O&M $1.2M/MW-yr, facility capex $10M/MW. Leased/colocation (all other sites, incl. Vineland build-to-suit and Bethune): power + colocation $2.8M/MW-yr, rent fixed for the lease term (Harlow 10 yrs, AIB 12 yrs, others 5-15 yrs) even if capacity is idle; no facility capex. Other opex 27% of revenue (bear 30%, bull 24%).
inputs_detail.derivation: Q1-26 letter: owned capacity 3 GW across five sites (>75% of contracted power), so charging colocation on owned MW while also capitalising the facility double-counted (inventory F2). Owned power ~$0.08/kWh x 8,760 h = $0.7M/MW plus ~$0.5M O&M/insurance/property tax. Facility $10M/MW: Mega Or ~$880M for 80 MW IT (~$11M/MW) and Azur ~EUR1.5B for 240 MW (~$7.3M/MW). Leased: research note power ~$0.9M + colocation ~$1.8M per MW-yr (~16% yield on a $10M/MW shell). Directions: Nebius pays rent to DataOne, Azur, Mega Or, Kao, Vantage, MERLIN, Greenergy, AIB, Ark, Equinix, Verne, Patmos; AIB prepayments are prepaid rent (timing only).

inputs_detail.value: IT $21.25M/MW for every site; plus facility $10M/MW for owned sites (half of 2027-start facilities assumed spent in the 2026 stub); sensitivities IT -/+12% ($22M/$28M all-in equivalent) and facility $8.5M/$12M
inputs_detail.derivation: Round 3 used $25M/MW all-in on every MW. Now IT capex = 85% x $25M (the round-3 IT share, consistent with the letter's 1y10m payback and the 2026 guide of $20-25B for 0.8-1.0 GW connected) and the facility is added only where Nebius owns the building. Owned all-in $31.25M/MW; leased $21.25M/MW plus rent. 2027 capex $27.8B (base, probability-weighted).

inputs_detail.input: Economic life, refresh capex and D&A
inputs_detail.value: Base economic life 6 yrs (5 and 7 as sensitivities); refresh at age 6 = 85% x $25M/MW (IT share at new-cohort cost); 10% salvage of original IT cost; tax D&A 85% of capex over 5 yrs (book life), 15% over 20 yrs
inputs_detail.derivation: Nebius books servers over 5 yrs (4->5 from 1 Jan 2026, 'updated information and usage patterns', 20-F). CoreWeave 6 yrs (no salvage disclosed), IREN HPC hardware 5 yrs (FY26 10-K R68, verified; round 3 wrongly said 6), Lambda 5, hyperscalers 5-6 (fact-check). A100s (2020) still rent at 23-39% of launch above power+colo; CoreWeave signed an A100 contract into 2029 and re-booked H100s within 5%; against it, Amazon cut some servers 6->5 yrs and Nvidia ships yearly. 6 yrs is the refresh point because by age 6 the base curve leaves revenue at ~46% of the vintage rate while a refresh earns the new rate; tails stay cash-positive. Salvage 10% (CCIR A100 80GB 21% at 5.8 yrs, less removal). Refresh only if the unit IRR (blended site cost $1.6M/MW) beats WACC: 20.5% base, 4.7% bear (bear cohorts run off; leased rent continues to lease end). Megawatt-constrained check (supervisor): after the named sites are built (2032) MW binds; on my model a 5-yr refresh is still worth less ($125) than 6 ($144) because the refresh NPV per MW is thinner than the value of sweating the tail.

inputs_detail.value: 3.0% / 22% / explicit to 2050: site builds 2027-32, refresh at age 6, then 3%/yr generic growth (owned-site cost) from 2033; terminal on normalised 2039-50 FCF
inputs_detail.derivation: Long-run nominal growth below the 5.29% risk-free; blended Dutch/US statutory rates (NOLs ignored; tax shields used group-wide). Generic growth after 2032 is not tied to an inventory site and is worth ~$3.7/share; terminal FCF is the growth-adjusted average of the last 12 years to smooth refresh lumps, all discounted at WACC.

inputs_detail.value: 12.5% (Ke 13.1%) for uncontracted, post-contract, pipeline and terminal cash flows; sensitivities 13.5% (ERP 5.0%) and 12.0% (ERP 4.14%)
inputs_detail.derivation: Following Damodaran's method: rf = 5.29% 10-yr UST (2026-09-30) less 0.23% US default spread = 5.06%; US ERP 4.46% (Damodaran, Jan-2026). Ke = 5.06% + 1.8 x 4.46% = 13.1%. Beta 1.8 is judgment (reported 5Y beta 1.46 contaminated by Yandex-era history; 106% realized vol, pure AI-capex exposure). After-tax Kd ~5.5% (secured SOFR+2.50%, converts 0.5-4.5% coupons), debt ~8% of capital. Round 1's 5.0% ERP is kept as a sensitivity because the 10-yr has risen ~50bp since Damodaran's January estimate.

inputs_detail.value: Microsoft 7.5%; Meta 2025 7.75%; Meta $12B dedicated 8.5%; Meta $15B backstop floor 9.0%; Q2-26 unrated deals 10.5%; PV-weighted IG rate ~7.8%
inputs_detail.derivation: Anchor: Nebius's only secured financing against an IG contract (most likely Meta 2025, inventory F12) costs SOFR 3.87% + 2.50% = 6.37% pre-tax (~5.0% after tax); Meta's 2031 notes yield 4.55%, the pure counterparty floor. An unlevered contract-level rate = ~75% secured debt (5.0-6.4%) + ~25% equity tranche at Ke 13.1% = ~7-8%. Microsoft (AAA, all tranches delivered by Aug-2026, so residual risk is SLA/termination) 7.5%; Meta 2025 (AA-, in servicing) 7.75%; Meta dedicated (not yet built, late-delivery fee discounts) 8.5%; backstop (contingent purchase obligation, clusters unspecified, price undisclosed) 9.0%; Q2-26 deals (private AI labs/quant fund, unrated, but ~70% with prepayments covering 50-60% of capex) 10.5%, midway to WACC. Only cash flows inside each term use these rates; re-lease, refresh and terminal flows use 12.5%.

inputs_detail.value: 0.95 late-2026/early-2027 colocation deliveries (Bethune phase 1 spare, Beit Shemesh, Masmiya); 0.9 Bethune phase 2, Estonia, Harlow, AIB, PA 260 MW, Independence 150 MW; 0.85 Madrid, Newport, Lappeenranta/Birmingham/Independence 2028 phases; 0.8 Lappeenranta 2029, PA +400; 0.75 Independence 2029, PA +340; 0.7 UK fourth site, Independence 2030; 0.65 PA/Independence 2031; 0.6 Independence 2032; 0.5 Oklahoma
inputs_detail.derivation: Higher where the building is host-funded and nearly complete or a binding lease/ESA exists (AIB 8-K, Kao 10-yr lease, PPL ESA), lower where power arrives later (Independence 'additional power by early 2029', PA 1,000+ MW by Nov-2029), where the site or MW is unconfirmed (UK fourth site, Oklahoma) and as cumulative funding needs grow (~$28B 2027 capex). Each slice's revenue, costs and capex are multiplied by its probability. All sites built (p=1) would add ~$8/share.

inputs_detail.input: Net cash at 9/30/26 pro forma (ex ITM converts)
inputs_detail.derivation: $8.04B cash at 6/30 + ~$5.68B net from Aug-26 converts + $0.775B secured facility + ~$2.5B Q3 operating cash (prepayments; >$9B guided for 2026) - ~$6.5B Q3 capex = ~$10.5B; + $2.8B if the remaining 12.3M ATM shares were sold at ~$230. Debt: $5.75B Aug-26 converts (OTM at $313/$325) + $0.775B secured + small current debt.
$5.98B deferred revenue at 6/30/26 plus net Q3 prepayments; subtracted because the DCF recognises that revenue without new cash.
28% of ClickHouse at $15B Jan-26 round = $4.2B, 25% private-stake haircut = $3.15B; +$0.5B for Toloka/Avride (judgment; Toloka cost basis $97M, Avride raised SAFEs).

271.86M A+B outstanding at 6/30/26 (note 14) + ~21M NVIDIA pre-funded warrants (in basic weighted 280.4M) + 15.8M Aug-26 exchange shares + 2.74M unvested Eigen shares + ~10M awards + ~50M in-the-money convert shares (65.4M anti-dilutive at 6/30 less the 15.8M exchanged; Sep-25 $3.16B x 7.2072/1,000 = 22.8M; Mar-26 ~23.8M at $183.22/$180.31; Jun-25 remainder ~3.9M) = 372M (supervisor confirmed ~370M); ITM converts are then excluded from debt. Added the 12.3M shares left on the ATM at 6/30 (Q3 usage undisclosed) as if fully sold, with ~$2.8B proceeds at ~$230 added to cash.

inputs_detail.value: bear 25% ($11), base 50% ($133 = avg of $114 and $152), bull 25% ($291); +$2.4 asset-light; split rate (single rate: $6 / $109-147 / $287)
inputs_detail.derivation: Base = uncontracted 2026-29 rates x1.0 and x1.15, base decay curve, site probabilities. Bull = x1.3, tight decay curve, IT capex -8%, other opex 24%, WACC 11.5%, long-run $13.7M, all named sites built (p=1). Bear = x0.85, supply-long curve, IT capex +8%, other opex 30%, long-run $13.0M: refresh IRR 4.7% < WACC, so no refresh, no uncontracted builds starting after 2029 and cohorts run off (leased rent paid to lease end). Contracts keep their prices in all scenarios. Per-share values rolled forward 12 months at Ke.

inputs_detail.value: +$2.4/share: 40% probability of ~200 MW partner capacity by 2028-29 earning a ~10% fee on ~$20M/MW revenue at 80% margin, 3% growth, at WACC
inputs_detail.derivation: July-2026 PR: initial partner arrangements signed (revenue share, licensing, committed capacity), no MW or dates. Partner-owned power, so it does not overlap any Nebius site MW. 0.4 x $2.6B (perpetuity at 12.5%-3%) discounted 2.25 yrs = ~$0.8B.

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: 4.2x EV/NTM sales (CoreWeave 4.1-4.9x at ~104% forward growth) on $23B NTM revenue at Oct-2027 = $96.6B EV, less $15.6B net debt, plus $3.65B stakes = $84.7B, divided by 384M shares

inputs_detail.input: NTM revenue at Oct-2027 (Q4-27 to Q3-28)
inputs_detail.derivation: Site model base: 0.3 x 2027 $13.7B + 0.7 x 2028 $27.9B = $23.7B (round 3's aggregate model had 2028 at $32.1B). The named-site schedule puts ~2.0 GW probability-weighted in service in 2028 vs ~2.8 GW in round 3's aggregate path, and the YE26 base is active (~0.57 GW), not connected, power. Small haircut toward consensus (2027 $12.30B) to $23B.

CoreWeave EV $94.88B over NTM revenue of $19.5B (market cap / forward P/S 2.5) = 4.9x, or $22.9B (0.25 x 2026 $12.87B + 0.75 x 2027 $26.26B consensus) = 4.1x, with consensus growth of ~104% into 2027. NBIS at Oct-2027 is forecast to grow ~100% NTM over TTM, so a similar growth profile; I take the low half of the 4.1-4.9x range because the multiple is applied a year later, after another year of GPU price deflation and with the 10-yr at 5.29%, partly offset by NBIS's lighter balance sheet (CoreWeave net debt $46B).
Start +$6.7B pro-forma net cash, less ~$22.3B FCF burn Q4-26 to Q3-27 from the site model base case (round 3 $18.8B; the increase is owned-site facility capex), assumed debt-funded.
28% of ClickHouse at $15B Jan-26 round = $4.2B, 25% private-stake haircut = $3.15B; +$0.5B for Toloka/Avride (judgment; Toloka cost basis $97M, Avride raised SAFEs).

271.86M A+B outstanding at 6/30/26 (note 14) + ~21M NVIDIA pre-funded warrants (in basic weighted 280.4M) + 15.8M Aug-26 exchange shares + 2.74M unvested Eigen shares + ~10M awards + ~50M in-the-money convert shares (65.4M anti-dilutive at 6/30 less the 15.8M exchanged; Sep-25 $3.16B x 7.2072/1,000 = 22.8M; Mar-26 ~23.8M at $183.22/$180.31; Jun-25 remainder ~3.9M) = 372M (supervisor confirmed ~370M); ITM converts are then excluded from debt. Added the 12.3M shares left on the ATM at 6/30 (Q3 usage undisclosed) as if fully sold, with ~$2.8B proceeds at ~$230 added to cash.

bear.story: AI-capex digestion or GPU price deflation: new-deal ACV per MW falls back toward the ~$12M 2026 base, capacity slips, and funding $22-28B/yr of capex leans on dilutive ATM and converts. The market re-rates NBIS to about 2x NTM sales and starts to price DCF-like cash-flow risk (my DCF bear case is ~$11: ~$28/share of signed-contract value, mostly Microsoft, offset by value-destroying uncontracted builds); a Redburn-style $84 target becomes the anchor. GPU-life angle: if Blackwell/Rubin supply turns plentiful and power gets cheaper, post-contract rents fall toward cash cost within 3-4 years (supply-long curve), refreshes stop earning the cost of capital and the DCF goes to option value.

base.story: Nebius brings ~1.0-1.1 GW into service in 2027 (Bethune, Israel, Estonia, UK, Mantsala 2, Lappeenranta and Birmingham first phases, Independence and Highridge starting), posts 2027 revenue of $13-14B and ~$24B NTM revenue by Oct-2027, with Microsoft and the first Meta dedicated tranches running on contract and ~55-60% adj. EBITDA margins as owned campuses come on. Capex of ~$28B is funded by prepayments, contract-secured debt at ~SOFR+250 and some ATM. Older cohorts keep renting after their contracts at falling prices. The multiple compresses to about 4x NTM sales as growth slows toward ~100%, so the stock ends a little below today's level with heavy volatility on the way.

bull.story: Q2-26 deal economics ($20-25M/MW, ~22-month payback) hold across >1GW deployed in 2027, short-term premium deals and auctions lift pricing, Vera Rubin ramps on time, and exit-2027 ARR exceeds $25B. The market holds 5-6x NTM sales and the Aug-2026 notes ($313-325 conversion prices) end up in the money. GPU-life angle: the tight market persists, expiring contracts re-price near original levels (CoreWeave's H100s within 5%, A100 into 2029), so each cohort earns for 6-7+ years. Site angle: every named site is delivered on schedule (Highridge 1,000+ MW by Nov-2029, Independence on its four-building plan), the Meta backstop clusters sell to third parties above the floor, and more IG contracts are financed at SOFR+250.

thesis_break_reason: At about $115 the equity is worth roughly $44B on ~384M diluted shares (~$56B EV at Oct-2027 net debt), about 2.4x the ~$23B NTM revenue path and below the Sep-2025 convert conversion price ($138.75). It sits below my site-based DCF at a 5-year life ($125) and at a 5.0% ERP ($126), level with the $14M long-run-rate case ($115) and the supply-long decay case ($118); the signed IG contracts alone are worth ~$28/share. Trading there would most likely mean something fundamental broke rather than ordinary 100%-vol noise: new-deal $/MW rolling back toward the $12M fleet base, post-contract re-leasing rents collapsing (supply glut), slippage on the owned campuses (Highridge 260 MW by Oct-2027, Independence, Birmingham) or the Meta dedicated tranches, or financing (ATM, converts, contract-secured debt) seizing up.

catalysts.event: Hyperscaler Q3 earnings and 2027 capex commentary (MSFT, META, GOOGL, AMZN)
CME/Silicon Data GPU compute futures launch: first market-traded forward curve for GPU-hour prices (a read on expected rental decay)
Q3-26 results (date estimated): ARR progress toward $7-9B YE26 guide, capex, prepayments, Q3 ATM usage
First Meta dedicated tranches ($12B, 5-yr) energize on Finland/US capacity; late-delivery fee discounts would show up here
Further contract-secured debt at ~SOFR+250 against Microsoft/Meta contracts (framework for >$40B), lowering funding cost vs ATM/converts
Formal 2027 guidance (management said 'later in 2026'): GW deployed, revenue, capex
NVIDIA FQ3 earnings and Blackwell/Vera Rubin supply commentary
Q4/FY26 results: whether the $7-9B ARR exit and $3.0-3.4B revenue guide were met
New convertible, ATM or asset-backed financings to fund >1GW/yr build (dilution vs. cheaper secured debt)
Vera Rubin NVL72 production ramp and pricing for next-gen capacity
Monetisation of ClickHouse stake (~28%) or Avride outside capital

key_uncertainties: Durability of the $20-25M/MW pricing on Q2-26 deals versus the ~$12M/MW 2026 base as GPU supply loosens: the site DCF runs from ~$11 (bear) to ~$291 (bull); with 2027-29 uncontracted vintages on Q2 terms it is $179; the long-run rate ($14M/$17M) moves it $115/$174
Capex per MW: IT -/+12% moves the DCF to $162/$127, owned facility $8.5M/$12M to $153/$134; the letter's 1y10m payback is still the main gap to spot
Discount rate: ERP 5.0% vs 4.14% moves the DCF from $126 to $155; splitting contracted cash flows at 7.5-10.5% adds only ~$4.6 because they are short (<=5.5 yrs) and net of capex, opex and tax
GPU economic life and re-leasing rents: 5/6/7-yr life gives $125/$144/$153; supply-long decay $118, tight $177

Site execution: Highridge PA (260 MW by Oct-2027, 1,000+ MW by Nov-2029), Independence (additional power by early 2029, on-site generation), Birmingham (lawsuits), Lappeenranta; all named sites built would add ~$8/share, the ~1 GW of the 5 GW contracted-power target not tied to a named site is excluded
Financing mix and dilution: ~384M diluted shares including ~50M ITM convert shares, 21M NVIDIA warrants and the remaining ATM, against $22-28B/yr capex needs
Customer concentration and counterparty quality (Microsoft, Meta, AI neolabs such as Reflection and Cohere) behind the $37.5B RPO
Sector multiple: CoreWeave at 4.1-4.9x EV/NTM sales sets the anchor for 60% of my fair value; a de-rating of the group passes straight through
Contract mapping: the Meta dedicated and backstop clusters' sites and MW are undisclosed (priced at $12M/$20M per MW the DCF is $141/$149); Microsoft is assumed to take all 300 MW at Vineland
reasoning: Round 4 (site coverage and split discounting). I rebuilt the DCF from the 25-site inventory: each site appears once, as slices with MW, energization, ownership and contract. Energized and contracted capacity carries its contract (Microsoft $17.4B to mid-2031 at Vineland; Meta 2025 $2.9B; Meta $12B dedicated from 2027; the Meta $15B backstop as a 5-yr floor on Birmingham phase 1; Q2-26 neolab deals), checked against the Meta and secured-facility 6-Ks and the AIB 8-K. Uncontracted and pipeline capacity is probability-weighted (0.5-0.95) net of its capex. Inventory flags fixed: F1 (site-built), F2 (owned sites pay power+O&M and carry facility capex instead of colocation rent), F3/F5 (Meta contracts and backstop), F6 (YE26 active ~0.57 GW, not 0.9 GW connected), F8 (split rates), F9 (lease rents fixed for their term), F10 (asset-light valued, Palantir capacity not double-counted). Contracted cash flows inside each term are discounted at 7.5-9.0% for Microsoft/Meta (anchored on the SOFR+2.50% = 6.37% facility and Meta's 4.55% 2031 notes, plus an equity tranche for delivery/SLA risk) and 10.5% for unrated Q2 deals; everything else at the 12.5% WACC. Bridge (weighted): round-3 $134 -> same cost convention on the site schedule $125 (fewer MW by 2028, active base, probabilities) -> owned-site cost fix $137 -> split rates $142 -> asset-light $144. Single-rate DCF $140. The split adds only ~$4.6 because the contracts are short and much of their revenue funds opex, tax and the capex for the Meta builds; the value still sits in post-contract and pipeline cash flows at WACC. EV/sales falls to $220 (NTM revenue $23B on the site path; net debt $15.6B with facility capex). Blended fair value $190 (was $204). Base scenario $210 (was $225), bear $88 (was $95), bull $400 unchanged; the ladder moves down ~1-2 points in the middle (P(>= $232) 0.465 -> 0.445). Thesis break stays at $115 (now below the 5-yr-life and ERP-5% DCFs). The 1-month ladder is unchanged: no new event falls in the window and the site work changes long-run value, not October's event set. GPU-life approach kept (contract price for the term, decay path, 6-yr refresh at full IT cost); facts corrected per the fact-check (IREN 5 yrs verified in its 10-K, CoreWeave salvage not disclosed, Nebius 20-F wording). Research this round: 5 fetches (Nebius $775M facility and Meta 6-Ks, AIB 8-K, NY Fed SOFR, IREN 10-K R68), no searches.

gpu_life.revenue_decay_path: Signed contracts at their price for their own term (Microsoft to mid-2031, Meta 5 yrs per order, backstop floor 5 yrs, Q2-26 deals ~2.5 yrs); uncontracted vintages 80% on 3-yr terms at the vintage rate. After the term revenue per MW = rate x 1.00/1.00/0.80/0.65/0.57/0.51/0.46/0.42 at ages 0-7; at age 6 GPUs retire (10% salvage) and the MW is refreshed at full IT cost ($21.25M/MW; the owned facility is not rebuilt) with a new 3-yr contract at the then-current vintage rate, only while the unit IRR beats WACC.

discounting.basis: Cash flows inside a signed contract's term are discounted at a contract-level rate: Microsoft (AAA, all tranches delivered) 7.5%, Meta 2025 (AA-, in servicing) 7.75%, Meta $12B dedicated (AA-, not yet built) 8.5%, Meta $15B backstop floor 9.0%; PV-weighted ~7.8%. Anchor: Nebius's $775M senior secured facility against one IG contract (probably Meta 2025) at SOFR 3.87% + 2.50% = 6.37% (6-K, 17 Jul 2026; NY Fed 1 Oct 2026), with Meta's own 2031 notes at 4.55% as the counterparty floor; a ~25% equity tranche at Ke 13.1% on top of ~75% secured debt gives ~7-8%, with +0.5-1.5pp for completion or contingency. Unrated Q2-26 deals (Reflection AI, Cohere, a neolab, a quant firm; ~70% with prepayments covering 50-60% of capex) 10.5%, midway to WACC. Post-contract re-lease, refresh, uncontracted pipeline, generic growth and terminal flows stay at the 12.5% WACC. Reconciliation (weighted, split, $/share): sites $149.5 (incl. asset-light $2.4) + post-2032 generic growth $3.7 + Q4-26 stub (incl. ~$7B capex) -$18.8 + net cash, stakes and deferred revenue $9.9 = $144. Contracted streams are worth ~$32/share (Microsoft $18, Meta 2025 $4, Meta dedicated $3, backstop $3, Q2 deals $4); splitting the rate adds ~$4.6 because these flows are short (<=5.5 yrs) and net of opex, tax and the Meta build capex.

The site path gives 2028 revenue of $27.9B (round 3 $32.1B); owned-site facility capex raises the Q4-26 to Q3-27 burn to $22.3B.
Lower NTM revenue on the site schedule and higher net debt pass through the multiple-driven base.
Same 2x NTM sales anchor on lower revenue and higher net debt; signed contracts (~$28/share in the bear DCF) limit the downside.
Fair value -$14 and base scenario -$15 shift the middle down ~2 points; tails move ~0.5-1 point.
